sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the north-west side of the Freehold business centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the upper right. Broad Street runs along the top of the sheet and West Main Street crosses it from left to right at mid-height. Throckmorton Street, with the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks laid in and beside it, runs down the right-hand side, and McLean Street leads off diagonally to the lower left, where Kiawa Avenue and Randolph Street branch from it. Between Broad and West Main the blocks hold mostly frame dwellings with stables and sheds, the Broad Street School (a cruciform brick building with a hot-steam heating and electric lighting note), the Second Reformed Church with hitching and auto stalls beside it, and further right the Gilbert Combs Co. coal yard with its trestle pockets and stable. The Municipal Building and 1st Fire Department, coloured as a fireproof building, stands on the north side of West Main Street, and the passenger station of the railroad lies east of it beside the tracks. On Throckmorton Street are a laundry, an auto sales building, a radiator shop and a long storage building, with a hydrant and water pipes marked in the streets. South of West Main Street the lots are deep and narrow, with dwellings facing the street and a row of narrow lots running back from McLean Street. Large parts of the lower left are blank, holding the compass and the scale of feet, and the sheet number labels in the margin point to adjoining sheets 3, 5, 6, 9 and 10.
notes: West Main is West Main Street, Throckmorton is Throckmorton Street, McLean is Mc Lean Street and Kiawa Avenue is Kiawah Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Throckmorton Street carries railroad tracks in its roadway; the Throckmorton / West Main point is a weak control point.

50 ft. Broad Street (top), West Main Street, Throckmorton Street, municipal building; one part. Configured by helper: sparse, 6 points (1 hand-picked Kiawa/McLean), rails in Throckmorton Street; Broad Street at the top edge.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the commercial centre of Freehold at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that north points toward the upper right. Broad Street runs along the top, Throckmorton Street with the railroad down the left edge, and Court Street rises from the middle of the sheet to Broad Street. West Main Street runs across the sheet from the left and becomes East Main Street on the right; South Street leaves it diagonally to the lower left and meets Mechanic Street at the bottom. The block between Broad and West Main Streets holds dwellings and stables at the top, Forman Park used for auto parking, St. Peters Episcopal Church with its chapel and rectory on Throckmorton Street, and, along West Main, a continuous row of stores with the Monmouth Democrat printing office, the Bank, the Post Office and the Freehold Trust Co. Beside the Court Street block stand the Monmouth County Jail, the record vaults and the Monmouth County Court House, drawn as fireproof buildings coloured pink, with the Strand Theatre and a large garage to the east along Lafalette Place. South of West Main Street the sheet shows the Orpheum Theatre, the Belmont Hotel, an American Hotel, banks, a transcript printing office, a press room and a garage with a cement floor, and a public market lot with auto and buggy stalls on the right. Railroad Hotel stands at the top left on Throckmorton Street. Water pipes and hydrants are marked in the streets, and the margin numbers refer to adjoining sheets 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 12.
notes: Lafalette Place is Lafayette Street in OpenStreetMap; the part of Main Street drawn as East Main here is still West Main Street in OpenStreetMap.
Throckmorton Street carries railroad tracks in its roadway, so the Throckmorton / West Main point is weak.
Court Street meets West Main Street in a wide open space; the control point at that junction was hand-picked and is approximate.

50 ft. Business district: Court Street, Lafayette Place, West and East Main Streets, South Street, Throckmorton, Mechanic; post office; one part. Configured by helper: Court/South/West Main hand-picked (wide open junction); rails in Throckmorton; Lafayette printed "LAFALETTE PL.".

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the blocks east and north-east of the Freehold business centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the upper right. Lafayette Place and Wayne Avenue run along the top, Hudson Street along the bottom, Sheriff Street on the left and Henry and Bennett Streets on the right edge. East Main Street crosses the middle of the sheet diagonally; where Spring Street comes down from the north it meets East Main and Centre Street, and Broadway branches off eastward, with a small triangular park between Broadway and East Main. North of Broadway the sheet shows the Freehold Gas Light Co. works, marked as a plant not operated with gas brought from Atlantic Highlands: storage and purifying buildings, a lime house, a disused gasometer and a large round gasometer holder beside Spring Street. Along West and East Main Street stand the Carnegie Library, a garage with cement floors, a motor storage and express building, a battery service station and a concrete-block garage, with dwellings and stores around them. The rest of the sheet is residential: frame dwellings with stables and auto sheds along Wayne Avenue, Broadway, Centre and Bennett Streets, and lots running back from Hudson Street, one reached by a private driveway. Water pipes are drawn in most streets, with fire hydrants and a fire alarm box at East Main Street near Centre Street. Parts of neighbouring sheets 3, 7, 8, 9, 12 and 13 adjoin along the edges.
notes: Broadway is Broadway Road in OpenStreetMap; Centre is Center Street; Lafayette Place is Lafayette Street.
The modern junction of Broadway Road, Center, East Main, Spring and West Main Streets is one node where the sheet draws two junctions; it was left out of the fit.
Freehold Gas Light Co. plant marked 'not operated', gas supplied from Atlantic Highlands.
50 ft. Pilot. Lafayette Place, Sheriff, Spring, Wayne Avenue, Henry, East Main, Broadway (now Broadway Road), Centre (Center Street), Hudson, Bennett; one part. Defaults found 8 points.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers a residential district in the west of Freehold, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the upper left. McLean Street crosses the top of the sheet, and West Main Street runs down the left side diagonally from the top to the lower left. Lincoln Place, labelled with the Institute, crosses the middle from West Main Street to Cottage Place on the right edge; Kiawa Avenue runs down the centre between McLean Street and Hull Avenue, which crosses the bottom, and Cottage Place runs down the right margin. Manalapan Avenue joins West Main Street from the left near the middle of the sheet. The blocks hold frame dwellings, most with stables or sheds, set on deep narrow lots, with two dwellings and a stable coloured as tile or brick near Lincoln Place. Lumber storage and a few auto sheds stand in the blocks south of Lincoln Place, and a building with a blue-bordered outline, probably a cement or stucco structure, lies west of Kiawa Avenue. A large area on the upper right is blank, holding the compass and the sheet's own label. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches are marked in West Main Street, McLean Street, Kiawa Avenue, Hull Avenue and Cottage Place, with hydrants at several corners. Adjoining sheet numbers 2, 6, 10 and 15 stand in the margins.
notes: McLean is Mc Lean Street, West Main is West Main Street, Kiawa Avenue is Kiawah Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Lincoln Place is lettered 'Lincoln Pl. (Institute)'.
The modern Cottage Place / Lincoln Place node does not match the drawn junction (17.8 m off) and was left out of the fit.
50 ft. McLean, Kiawa Avenue, Lincoln Place, Hull Avenue, West Main; one part. Configured by helper: Cottage Place/Lincoln Place junction excluded (detected 17.8 m off).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the blocks south of Throckmorton Street between South Street and Kiawa Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Throckmorton Street crosses the top corner, with Elm Street leaving it eastward near its junction with South Street, which runs down the right side of the sheet past Marcy Street. McLean Street crosses the middle from west to east and Randolph Street runs south from it to Lincoln Place, which, with Institute Street as its continuation, forms the bottom edge; Kiawa Avenue is cut by the left edge. The block between Throckmorton and McLean holds the St. Rose of Lima Parochial School, garages of hollow tile and concrete, a flour, feed and hay store, an auto and hitching shed and a sign painting shop, with dwellings along South Street. South of McLean Street stands St. Rose of Lima R.C. Church with its chapel and storage building. In the south-east corner is the Freehold Military School, drawn with its dormitories, recitation rooms and gymnasium, laundry and kitchen, beside a shooting gallery and a carpenter shop. The remaining lots, many of them deep and narrow, carry frame dwellings with stables and auto sheds, and blocks 2, 2B, 3 and 20 1/2 are numbered. The west half of the sheet is largely open land in long lots. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn in the streets. Neighbouring sheets 2, 3, 5, 7, 14 and 15 are indicated around the edges.
notes: Kiawa Avenue is Kiawah Avenue in OpenStreetMap; McLean is Mc Lean Street.
Few junctions are drawn in full: Lincoln Place and Kiawa Avenue lie along the sheet edges; the part rests on three detected junctions and is low confidence.
Marcy Street meets South Street about 25 m from McLean on the sheet but 9 m from it in OpenStreetMap; it was not used.
50 ft. Throckmorton, McLean, Randolph, South, Lincoln Place (Institute), St. Rose of Lima church and school, Freehold Military School; one part; few junctions, edge streets.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows the manufacturing and railroad district on the south-east side of Freehold's centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top. Mechanic Street crosses the upper part of the sheet from South Street on the left to Hudson Street, where it turns south-east toward the margin; Hudson Street rises diagonally to the upper right. South Street runs down the left edge, Elm Street crosses the middle, Conover Street runs down the centre and Marcy Street closes the bottom. Parker Street and Orchard Street appear at the lower right. The north side of Mechanic Street is occupied by Steiner and Son, Plant No. 6, with a stone-cutting works, the Model Mfg. Co. dress factory, and a long run of workshops and sheds on the upper left. South of Mechanic Street are dwellings, shops and stores, then a garage coloured as fireproof construction beside the Pennsylvania Railroad, the Sigmund Eisner and Sons shirt factory, a freight house and the William Patten wood and coal yard. The Pennsylvania R.R. and the C.R.R. of N.J. cross the sheet in broad bands of tracks from the left centre to the lower right. Below Elm Street the blocks are residential, with frame dwellings, auto sheds, a cabinet shop and a garage with auto sales for 40 cars, and a bottling works stands at the right. Water pipes and hydrants are marked in most streets. Adjoining sheets 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14 and 19 are named in the margins.
notes: Mechanic, South, Elm, Conover, Marcy and Hudson are Mechanic Street, South Street, Elm Street, Conover Street, Marcy Street and Hudson Street in OpenStreetMap; McLean Street is Mc Lean Street.
The modern Marcy Street / South Street junction does not match the drawn one (Marcy meets South 25 m from McLean on the sheet, 9 m in OpenStreetMap) and was left out of the fit.
50 ft. Mechanic, Elm, Marcy, Conover, South, railroad crossing; one part. Configured by helper: Marcy/South excluded; Mechanic Street kept (residuals about 2 m here).

sheet-8-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 8 is the main map, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It covers the east side of the borough from Hudson Street at the top to 2nd Street at the bottom, between Mechanic Street on the left and Centre Street on the right. The northern blocks between Hudson and Jackson Streets hold the Grammar School, the A. Brant lumber yard with its lumber sheds, yard office and coal storage, and rows of frame dwellings and boarding houses. South of Jackson Street the large A. & M. Karagheusian Inc. rug mill fills most of a block: weaving, winding, finishing and spinning rooms, a dye house, mill buildings, a boiler house and stores, drawn with its sprinkler and hydrant equipment and a long note on its fire protection. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the sheet below the mill on a curve, with sidings and the passenger depot, and on the left edge a siding to the Pennsylvania Railroad runs past a row of fertilizer storehouses and warehouses. Further south, Ford Avenue, 1st Street, Factory Street and 2nd Street are lined with small dwellings, junk yards and sheds, with a stone school building near Centre Street. Blocks 7, 19, 20, 27A, 27B, 27C, 28 and 210 are numbered. A boxed inset in the upper left corner (part 2) shows Lloyd Street at Ford Avenue. Sheets 4, 7, 12 and 13 adjoin.
notes: Centre is Center Street in OpenStreetMap.
Both Mechanic Street junctions on this part lay 4 to 5 m from a fit to the other points; Mechanic Street was left out (RMSE 2.9 to 0.6 m).
A. & M. Karagheusian Inc. rug mill fills the block south of Jackson Street.

50 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (Hudson, Jackson, Centre, 1st, 2nd, Factory, Ford Avenue, C.R.R. of N.J., A. & M. Karagheusian rug mill); 2 inset top left, Lloyd Street at Ford Avenue (Wm. Richter embroidery factory), drawn with north to the right.

sheet-8-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 8 is a small boxed inset in the upper left corner of the sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right, as its own north arrow shows. It shows the east end of Ford Avenue where it meets Lloyd Street, on the eastern edge of the borough, away from the main map of the sheet. Ford Avenue runs up the inset and Lloyd Street crosses it near the bottom. North of Lloyd Street, on the west side of Ford Avenue, is a row of small frame dwellings with outbuildings in block 210. South of Lloyd Street, in block 211, stands the Wm. Richter, Inc. embroidery factory, a two-storey building with a heater room, lit and powered by electricity and heated by hot air, marked as closed at the time of survey. A water pipe runs along Ford Avenue. The inset holds a single street junction, so it is placed from that one point with the sheet's scale and the direction of north measured from its streets.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked junction (Ford Avenue / Lloyd Street) with the sheet scale and north from the drawn streets; low confidence.
Wm. Richter, Inc. embroidery factory marked closed at time of survey.

50 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (Hudson, Jackson, Centre, 1st, 2nd, Factory, Ford Avenue, C.R.R. of N.J., A. & M. Karagheusian rug mill); 2 inset top left, Lloyd Street at Ford Avenue (Wm. Richter embroidery factory), drawn with north to the right.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the north-west edge of Freehold's centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the upper right. Monmouth Avenue forms the top edge, Broad Street the bottom edge, Stokes Street the left side and Throckmorton Street, with the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks beside it, the right side; George Street enters Stokes Street from the left. A row of frame dwellings with stables lies along the south side of Monmouth Avenue. The middle of the sheet is taken up by the J. H. Bawden and Co. iron foundry, a group of fireproof buildings (pink) including the pattern storage, engine and rattler rooms and polishing and machine shops, with flask sheds, a woodworking shop, a sand and brick store and a coal and coke yard, and a cattle pen beside the tracks. Further south, along the railroad, stand the County Farmers Exchange warehouse and the Monmouth fertilizer works, a lumber shed and the Gilbert Combs Co. lumber, coal and building materials yard with open lumber piles and an office. A freight house with a platform lies by the tracks near Broad Street. West of the large open middle are long narrow lots, mostly empty, with a few dwellings, sheds and stables on Stokes Street. The compass stands near the centre and large parts of the sheet are blank, with adjoining sheets 2, 10, 11, 12 and 18 named in the margins.
notes: Stokes is Stokes Street, Broad is Broad Street, Throckmorton is Throckmorton Street and George Street is East George Street in OpenStreetMap.
Rail crossings on Throckmorton Street give weaker control, as the tracks lie in the street.
50 ft. Monmouth Avenue, Stokes, Throckmorton, Broad, Pennsylvania R.R. and passenger station area, large open lots; one part; sparse. Configured by helper: sparse, 6 points (2 rail crossings).

sheet-10-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 10 is the main map, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It covers the south-west quarter of Freehold from Stokes Street at the top to Park Avenue, also lettered Fair Ground Road, near the bottom, and from Monmouth Avenue and Ann Street on the left to West Main Street on the right. Manalapan Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally; George Street runs north from it to Club Place and Stokes Street, and continues south of it to Yard Avenue and Park Avenue; Broad Street runs the full height of the sheet. The blocks are residential, with frame dwellings and stables on long lots, and blocks 61, 62, 63, 66, 67, 115 and 116 are numbered. Along West Main Street stand the Freehold First Baptist Church and the Freehold M.E. Church, and near Broad Street a Christian Science reading room. In the upper left corner, beside Monmouth Avenue, are the Colonial Pickle Works, marked as having no power. Below Park Avenue the sheet shows the Freehold Driving Association and Country Club grounds: a half-mile track, a grand stand with cement floors, a judges' stand, barns and the Freehold Country Club house. Heavy lines separate this part from a boxed inset of the Moreau Plant Co. greenhouses (part 2) and from the strip along West Main Street at Barkalow Avenue (part 3) on the left. Sheets 2, 5, 9 and 15 adjoin.
notes: George north of Manalapan Avenue is East George Street in OpenStreetMap, south of it West George Street.
Park Avenue (Fair Ground Road) junctions lay several metres off and were left out: the modern Park Avenue (NJ 33 Business) does not follow the 1923 line here (RMSE 6.0 to 1.3 m without it).
Freehold Driving Association and Country Club half-mile track below Park Avenue.

100 ft. Three parts: 1 main map (Monmouth Avenue, George, Club Place, Manalapan Avenue, Broad, Yard Avenue, Ann, West Main, Park Avenue / Fair Ground Road, Freehold Driving Association track); 2 inset top left, Moreau Plant Co. greenhouses (no street); 3 West Main Street at Barkalow Avenue, Moreau Plant Co. and Maplewood Cemetery, left of the heavy line.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Moreau Plant Co. greenhouses, heating plant and water tank (no street or feature shared with the modern data or another sheet; the sheet says only '100 ft to 150 ft W. Main St., see below'; needs a parcel or building corner of the greenhouse site, if one survives).

sheet-10-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 10 is the strip on the left of the sheet between two heavy lines, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It shows West Main Street running south-west out of town and Barkalow Avenue leaving it to the east, an area separate from the main map of the sheet. Between the two streets lies the property of the Moreau Plant Co., block 65, with a row of sheds and a few small buildings; a note says the greenhouses lie 100 feet beyond and refers to the inset above (part 2). West of West Main Street are frame dwellings with outbuildings in blocks 10 and 117, and at the lower left the edge of Maplewood Cemetery. Block 228 lies south of Barkalow Avenue and block 53 on the right beyond the heavy line. A water pipe runs along West Main Street. The part holds only the junction of West Main Street and Barkalow Avenue, so it is placed from that one point with the sheet's scale and the direction of north measured from West Main Street.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked junction (Barkalow Avenue / West Main Street) with the sheet scale and north from the drawn streets; low confidence.
The Moreau Plant Co. greenhouses are drawn as a separate inset (part 2) that could not be placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Moreau Plant Co. greenhouses, heating plant and water tank (no street or feature shared with the modern data or another sheet; the sheet says only '100 ft to 150 ft W. sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 shows the north-west part of Freehold at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north points toward the upper right and marked 'Scale 100 ft. to an inch' beside the compass. Monmouth Avenue closes the bottom of the sheet and Throckmorton Street, with the railroad on its west side, runs up the centre; Court Street forms the right edge. On the left Stokes Street runs diagonally from Monmouth Avenue up through the district, crossed by Bowne, Vought and Lenoir Avenues and by Thomas and William Streets, and Bannard Street and Trenton Road run beside the railroad lines. The Rhea road (Township Road) crosses the upper right diagonally, with Avenue C, Avenue B and Avenue A, Craig and David Streets forming a grid of blocks east of Throckmorton Street. The district is mainly residential, with small frame dwellings on narrow lots, many marked with lot letters and numbers. Industrial buildings stand beside the railroad: White and Snyder threshing and pressing works, the Electric Change Machine Co., and the Stokes Bros. file and rasp works, drawn as fireproof (pink). On the east side are the 2nd Baptist Church (Colored), H. F. Soden and Bro. planing mill, an M. E. Church (Colored), a bottling works and a public school. Large areas in the upper centre and right are open, with streets shown only as dashed lines. A Pennsylvania Railroad siding curves across the left centre. Adjoining sheets 9, 12 and 15 and block numbers 102 to 114 and 201 to 206 appear on the sheet.
notes: Haley Avenue is Haley Street, Lenoir Avenue and Vought Avenue are unchanged in OpenStreetMap, and Court is Court Street.
Court Street (Court / Haley 4.8 m, Court / Rhea 10 m off) and the Rhea road were left out of the fit because their modern lines are displaced from the drawn ones.
The sheet is at 100 feet to an inch.

100 ft. Northwest: Trenton, Rhea, Avenue A, Avenue C, Bannard, Thomas, William, Stokes, Haley, Pennsylvania R.R.; one part. Configured by helper: Court and Rhea (Township Road) left out (junctions 3.5 to 10 m off).

sheet-12-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 12 is the main map, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It covers the north side of the town centre from Murray and Henry Streets at the top right to Throckmorton Street along the bottom, and from Haley Avenue on the left edge to Broadway, Wayne Avenue and Lafayette Place on the right. Spring Street crosses the upper middle from west to east over a brook, and Sheriff Street runs below it. Schanck Street and Monument Place cross the left half diagonally, bounding Monmouth Park, in which the Monmouth Battle Monument is drawn. Court Street crosses the sheet below the park, and Broad Street runs south from it to Throckmorton Street. The lower blocks hold dwellings, the yard and sheds of a lumber company near Broad Street, and at the lower left the coal, lime and feed yard of D. V. Perrine beside the railroad sidings near Throckmorton Street. Along the top right are dwellings on Murray Street, Henry Street and Wayne Avenue, and a sewage pumping station near Spring Street. Much of the land west of Sheriff and north of Court Street is open, in large numbered blocks (5, 6, 8, 55, 56, 109, 118, 119). A heavy line marks off a boxed area in the upper left corner (part 2), drawn at its own orientation. Sheets 3, 4, 9, 11 and 13 adjoin.
notes: Broadway is Broadway Road in OpenStreetMap; Haley Avenue is Haley Street; Lafayette Place is Lafayette Street; Monument Place is now part of Monument Street.
Schanck Street met Court Street in 1923; the modern Monument Street junctions did not fit the drawn ones (residuals 4 to 6 m) and Monument Street was left out.
Monmouth Battle Monument in Monmouth Park.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (Murray, Broadway, Henry, Wayne Avenue, Spring, Sheriff, Schanck, Monument Place, Monmouth Park, Court, Lafayette Place, Broad, Haley Avenue, Throckmorton); 2 boxed top left: Liberty (Mount Avenue), Bennett, 1st, 2nd, 3rd, Bond Avenue, Centre, Lloyd.

sheet-12-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 12 is the boxed area in the upper left corner of the sheet, separated from the main map by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north nearly straight up, as its own arrow shows. It covers the small grid of streets on the east side of Freehold, between Liberty Street, also lettered Mount Avenue, at the top and Centre Street at the bottom, crossed by 1st, 2nd and 3rd Streets, with Bennett Street and Bond Avenue running between them and Lloyd Street at the right. The blocks, numbered 26A, 26B, 27C, 29, 123, 126 and 127, are almost entirely residential: rows of small frame dwellings, many of them two storeys, with sheds and stables on narrow lots, and a few outbuildings of brick. A note along Centre Street marks frame dwellings opposite, and the Central Railroad of New Jersey is noted along the left edge. Water pipes run in Liberty, Bond and Centre Streets and in 1st and 3rd Streets, with fire hydrants at the corners and a fire alarm box at Centre Street. Sheets 8 and 13 adjoin this part.
notes: Bond Avenue is Bond Street in OpenStreetMap; Centre is Center Street; Liberty is Liberty Street.
Drawn at its own orientation, about 20 degrees from the main map of the sheet.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (Murray, Broadway, Henry, Wayne Avenue, Spring, Sheriff, Schanck, Monument Place, Monmouth Park, Court, Lafayette Place, Broad, Haley Avenue, Throckmorton); 2 boxed top left: Liberty (Mount Avenue), Bennett, 1st, 2nd, 3rd, Bond Avenue, Centre, Lloyd.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the north-east side of Freehold at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north points toward the upper left. Broadway runs down the left centre from Robertsville Road at the top to Henry Street, where it joins East Main Street; East Main Street runs diagonally to the upper right, and Jackson Street runs down the right side from East Main Street to Centre Street at the bottom. Hudson Street runs down the middle of the lower part, crossed by Bennett Street and Centre Street. Lockwood Avenue, Fulton and Murray Streets branch from Broadway on the left, and Liberty Street and Bennett Street appear on the right edge. The upper left holds long narrow lots and a large open tract labelled Public School Athletic Field. Along Broadway and East Main Street are frame dwellings with stables, a B.P.O.E. building, and a row of fireproof dwellings marked as brick. East of Jackson Street stand A. and M. Karagheusian Inc., the rug mill's storage and office buildings, the Standard Oil Co. with its gas and oil tanks, a coal pile and a tool house, beside the C.R.R. of N.J. line down the right edge. At the bottom are the Freehold High School with its play grounds, a greenhouse, and rows of dwellings along Centre Street and Hudson Street. Water pipes of 3, 4 and 6 inches are marked, with hydrants at several corners. Adjoining sheets 4, 8 and 12 are named in the margins, and block numbers 54, 58, 59 and 120 to 122 appear.
notes: Broadway is Broadway Road, Centre is Center Street and E. Main is East Main Street in OpenStreetMap; Fulton and Murray are Fulton Street and Murray Street.
100 ft. North: Fulton, Murray, Lockwood, Broadway, Robertsville Road, Henry, Monument, Schanck, public school athletic field; one part. Configured by helper: 11 points, north toward the upper left.

sheet-14-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 14 is the main map, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north nearly straight up. It covers the south-east of Freehold from Marcy Street at the top to Vredenburgh Avenue near the bottom, and from Randolph Street and Lincoln Place on the left to Orchard Street, marked not opened, on the right. South Street runs down the left part of the sheet, crossed by Lincoln Place and its continuation Institute Street, Clinton Street, Hull Avenue, Union Avenue, Brinckerhoff Avenue and Jerseyville Avenue, which runs diagonally to the south-east. Conover, Washington and Parker Streets run north to south through the middle. The sheet is almost entirely residential: frame dwellings with stables and auto sheds on long lots, densest along Marcy, Conover and Parker Streets at the top and along South Street and Union Avenue, with an auto body building near South Street. Large blocks such as 20, 21, 22, 213, 221, 222, 225, 226 and 227 are only partly built, and some streets are marked not opened. A boxed inset at the lower right (part 2) shows South Street at Barkalow Avenue, further south. The tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad cross the upper right corner. Sheets 6, 7 and 15 adjoin.
notes: Vredenburgh Avenue is Vredenberg Avenue in OpenStreetMap; McLean Street is Mc Lean Street.
Orchard Street is marked not opened.
The detected Clinton Street / South Street junction was 50 ft off the drawn one and was excluded.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (Marcy, Conover, Parker, Orchard, Lincoln Place / Institute, Clinton, Hull Avenue, South, Washington, Union Avenue, Brinckerhoff Avenue, Jerseyville Avenue, Vredenburgh Avenue); 2 boxed inset lower right, South Street at Barkalow Avenue.

sheet-14-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 14 is a boxed inset in the lower right corner of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing up. It shows South Street at its junction with Barkalow Avenue, south of the main map of the sheet. South Street runs up the inset with a water pipe along it, and a road lettered only 'Road' crosses near the top. The blocks, numbered 222, 227 and 228, hold a scattering of frame dwellings, two storeys high, with auto sheds and outbuildings, and the sides of the inset are marked 'no exposure'. The inset holds one street junction, so it is placed from that point with the sheet's scale and the direction of north measured from South Street.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked junction (Barkalow Avenue / South Street) with the sheet scale and north from the drawn South Street; low confidence.
The road at the top of the inset is lettered only 'Road'; it may be an early line of Park Avenue, which crosses South Street about 180 m north of Barkalow Avenue today, further than drawn.

sheet-15-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 15 is the upper half of the sheet, above a heavy line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north straight up. It covers the blocks south of West Main Street between Yard Avenue on the left and Clinton Street on the right. West Main Street crosses the upper left corner diagonally; Hull Avenue and Brinckerhoff Avenue leave it and run south-east across the sheet, crossed by Kiawa Avenue, Cottage Place and Randolph Street, and Lincoln Place cuts the upper right corner. Along West Main Street stand a Presbyterian church and a veterinary building among dwellings. The rest is residential: frame dwellings with stables and auto sheds along Hull Avenue and on the short streets, and large, mostly empty blocks, numbered 64, 65, 134, 213, 221 and 222, south of Brinckerhoff Avenue. A ball ground with a grand stand is drawn in block 213 near Lincoln Place. Some street extensions are marked not opened. The lower half of the sheet (part 2) shows another area at its own orientation. Sheets 5, 6, 10 and 14 adjoin.
notes: Kiawa Avenue is Kiawah Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy horizontal line: 1 upper (West Main, Yard Avenue, Hull Avenue, Kiawa Avenue, Brinckerhoff Avenue, Cottage Place, Lincoln Place, Randolph, Clinton), north up; 2 lower (Manalapan Avenue, Lenoir Avenue, Ward, Vought Avenue, Bowne Avenue, Stokes, Monmouth Avenue, Joseph Brakeley Inc.), north toward upper right.

sheet-15-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 15 is the lower half of the sheet, below a heavy line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the upper right. It shows the industrial and residential area along Manalapan Avenue on the west side of Freehold, between Lenoir Avenue at the top and Monmouth Avenue at the bottom, with Ward Street and Stokes Street crossing Vought Avenue and Bowne Avenue. Most of the upper half is taken by the cannery of Joseph Brakeley Inc.: pea houses, can warehouses, the factory with its cookers, a machine shop, a filter house, box shop and a large warehouse, with a long note on its watchman, power, water supply and fire equipment, and across the siding its workmen's quarters and a restaurant. A siding to the Pennsylvania Railroad runs diagonally through the plant on a coal trestle. South of Bowne Avenue stand the Chas. Sandberg children's underwear factory and the Tennent Products Co. food products building. The blocks east of Ward Street, numbered 50, 50 1/2 and 52, are lined with frame dwellings and stables, and the lower left of the part is blank, block 53. Sheets 10 and 11 adjoin.
notes: Ward is Ward Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Joseph Brakeley Inc. cannery with workmen's quarters on a siding of the Pennsylvania Railroad.
The Bowne Avenue / Manalapan Avenue junction lay 19 m from the fit and was rejected.
